title: Language Feature Stability
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of language feature stability using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates language feature stability.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Language Feature Stability** as part of **Advanced Kotlin Language Features**. Apply language feature stability by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Stable Features, Experimental and Preview Features, Opt-In Requirements and Migration Planning—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
